title: XLuminA computationally discovers a super-resolution microscopy blueprint combining two optical principles
summary: The XLuminA differentiable optical-design system rediscovered established STED beam shaping and optical-vortex approaches, then identified a previously unreported experimental blueprint combining principles from both to produce sub-diffraction imaging in the study’s computational model. This is a specific theoretical/optical-design result, not a report of an independently built and experimentally validated microscope implementing the new blueprint.
ai_technology: XLuminA auto-differentiating optical experiment-design framework; transformer-based code-generation model used in the discovery workflow
organization: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light; Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg

evidence.tested: The XLuminA differentiable optical-design system rediscovered established STED beam shaping and optical-vortex approaches, then identified a previously unreported experimental blueprint combining principles from both to produce sub-diffraction imaging in the study’s computational model.
evidence.unknown: The novel design is established through computational optical modeling and simulation; the paper does not report physical construction or experimental validation of this specific blueprint. The three rediscovered designs are prior work and are not counted as new. Interpret as a computationally proposed optical design, not a demonstrated imaging instrument or biological discovery.
evidence.ai_role: AI-guided computational search generated and evaluated candidate optical experimental designs; numerical simulations identified a previously unreported combination of optical principles with predicted sub-diffraction capability. Researchers analyzed and interpreted the design.
